speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty with hand movement; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what activity was happening when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The patient's history of thumb and wrist pain radiating to the elbow, exacerbated by holding an infant, is classic for this condition, likely triggered by the fall six months ago which caused tendon irritation that has since become chronic.
